title: Nagelsmann quits as Germany coach after early World Cup 2026 exit
facts: Julian Nagelsmann agreed to step down as head coach of the Germany national football team.
Julian Nagelsmann's departure followed Germany's elimination from the 2026 World Cup by Paraguay.
Paraguay defeated Germany 4-3 on penalty kicks in the World Cup knockout stage.
Julian Nagelsmann had a contract with the German Football Association through the 2028 European Championship.
Bernd Neuendorf serves as President of the German Football Association (DFB).
Julian Nagelsmann was offered a seven-million-euro severance package to leave his post.
Julian Nagelsmann is the second national coach in German football history to be forced to step down.
Hansi Flick was the first German national coach forced to step down in 2023.
Germany was eliminated in the group stages of both the 2018 and 2022 World Cup tournaments.
Germany has not won a World Cup knockout match since the 2014 final against Argentina.
The German Football Association identified Jurgen Klopp as their preferred successor to Nagelsmann.
Jurgen Klopp publicly confirmed he is fundamentally willing to manage the Germany national team.
Jurgen Klopp left his managerial role at Liverpool in 2024.
Jurgen Klopp currently serves as global head of football for Red Bull.
Jurgen Klopp's contract with Red Bull includes a release clause permitting him to accept the Germany national team position.
